newsitem.title: GERMANY: Firmer Bunds seen capped by dmk fears, U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: Firmer Bunds seen capped by dmk fears, U.S. data.

text.p: German Bunds firmed in early trade on Wednesday as investors recognised that the debt market was no longer overbought.

But dealers said the potential for gains was limited by the fear of a further mark weakening and because investors were waiting for U.S. June consumer prices, business inventories and capacity utilisation later today.

September Bunds rose as high as 102.53, up 25 basis points from Tuesday's close, before paring gains to trade at 102.38 by 0750 GMT, up 10 basis points. They have technical resistance at 102.67 and support at 102.15 and 101.98, dealers said.

Downside risks for Bunds remained as the mark was likely to keep weakening until central banks took concrete action like coordinated intervention, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell wrote in a note to investors. "However, it is important to recognise that Bunds and Bobls are no longer overbought while the Deutschemark is deeply oversold on a technical basis.
"As such, the risks of a pronounced short squeeze somewhere in here are also quite noticeable."
The mark's steep depreciation has hit the short-end of the German debt market by raising fears the Bundesbank may increase interest rates.
But economists still regard a rate rise soon as unlikely given the absence of inflationary pressures and the weakness of consumer demand and domestic investment.
